claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child:

**How old is your child?**

To help determine eligibility, I need to know which age category your child falls into:

- **Under 16 years old**
- **16 to 19 years old**
- **20 years old or over**

Please let me know the age (or age range) of the child you're inquiring about. Also, if you have multiple children, I can assess each one for you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 9 years old. I live here in the UK and Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's very helpful. So you have **Alex, who is 9 years old** and lives with you in the UK.

Since Alex is **under 16 years old**, let me continue with the next step of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

Since Alex is 9 years old, this is typically not applicable, but I need to confirm: Is Alex engaged in any paid work? If not, just let me know "no" to confirm they're not in paid work.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 9, so he's just at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected for a 9-year-old. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I need to confirm: Is Alex receiving **Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)** or **Universal Credit** in their own name? 

For a 9-year-old, this is unlikely, but I need to check: Is Alex receiving either of these benefits?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a kid, so nothing like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT in an apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is only 9 years old and still in school, this is straightforward - Alex wouldn't be in an apprenticeship. Can you confirm that Alex is **not in an apprenticeship**?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's only 9, so he's just doing normal primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Let me move forward to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to check your residency status:**

You mentioned you live in the UK with Alex. To confirm your eligibility, I need to understand your residency situation better. Can you tell me which of the following applies to you?

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common situation)

2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**

3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (and if so, I'll need to check further details about your work, studies, or resources)

4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** (in certain qualifying countries)

Which of these best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I've been here all along, nothing complicated like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's straightforward. Since you normally live in the UK, you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means one of the following:

1. **You live with Alex** (which you've already confirmed - Alex lives with you at home)

2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - meaning you pay for things like food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents, or other essentials

3. **You make maintenance payments** under a court order or agreement towards Alex's care

Since you've already told me Alex lives with you at home, you clearly meet the responsibility requirement. Let me confirm: **You live with Alex and are responsible for his care and upkeep - is that correct?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. Alex lives with me and I take care of him - I pay for everything he needs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear - you're responsible for Alex. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

I need to check if there's another person (such as the other parent, grandparent, or guardian) who is currently claiming or intending to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

- **Is no one else claiming for Alex?**
- **Is someone else claiming, but you've both agreed who should claim?**
- **Is there a dispute about who should claim?**

Which applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear - you're the only person claiming for Alex. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Where is Alex living?**

I need to check if any special circumstances apply:

- **Is Alex in hospital?**
- **Is Alex in residential care?**
- **Is Alex fostered?**
- **Is Alex living normally at home with you?**

Based on what you've told me, I believe Alex is living normally at home with you - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct. Alex is living at home with me - just a normal situation, nothing special.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final question: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council not paying for Alex's housing or upkeep? This would typically be the case in a normal family situation where you're providing and paying for everything yourself.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything. I pay for everything myself - his accommodation, food, clothes, all of it.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the final check. Let me process your eligibility now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I have all the information I need. Let me provide you with your final eligibility decision.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You're **ELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit

---

### Your Result:

**✓ ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

---

### Why You're Eligible:

Alex meets all the requirements:
- ✓ Alex is 9 years old (under 16)
- ✓ Not working
- ✓ Not receiving benefits in his own right
- ✓ Not in an apprenticeship
- ✓ Living with you at home
- ✓ You normally live in the UK
- ✓ You're responsible for Alex's care and upkeep
- ✓ No one else is claiming for Alex
- ✓ The council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance

---

### Next Steps:

To claim Child Benefit, you need to:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Check the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some of the benefit (this doesn't prevent you from claiming, but it's important to be aware of)

**Payments** are made every 4 weeks by default, or weekly in certain circumstances (such as if you're a single parent).

For more information and to apply, visit: [www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)

---

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
